name: vPhone Workstation
tagline: A native macOS app for managing virtual iPhones — browse, create, and boot iOS research VMs
description: vPhone Workstation is a native macOS app for managing virtual iPhones, letting you browse, create, and boot iOS research virtual machines from a single window. It is a SwiftUI front-end for vphone-cli, the command-line tool that boots virtual iPhones on Apple's Virtualization.framework using PCC research VMs. The app provides a VM library with live running/stopped state, iOS and cloudOS build info, and search; a detail overview showing build, variant, CPU, memory, disk, network, device, and UDID at a glance; and full lifecycle controls to start, stop, and bring the running iPhone window to the front. It also supports clone, rename, export to .tar.xz, and delete, plus a create wizard that walks through name, variant (Less, Regular, Developer, Jailbreak, Experimental), firmware pairing, and resources with live step-by-step progress streamed from vphone-cli. Host readiness checks ensure vphone-cli is present and the environment is suitable for running research VMs.
highlights: Manage and boot iOS research VMs from a single native macOS window
SwiftUI front-end for vphone-cli built on Apple's Virtualization.framework with PCC research VMs
VM library with live state, search, and a detail overview of build, variant, CPU, memory, disk, and UDID
Full lifecycle controls including start, stop, clone, rename, export (.tar.xz), and delete
Create wizard with variant selection, firmware pairing, and live streamed progress from vphone-cli
curatorNote: A clean, well-designed GUI layer over the excellent vphone-cli, making iOS research VMs approachable. The focus on a professional library/detail UI and a guided create wizard with live progress turns a niche command-line research workflow into something a much wider audience can actually use.
